conclusions: All original short checks pass; no 600-second capacity qualification or #92 closure. Earlier failed receipts remain unchanged.
ARM rendered 553/574 → 551/562 with static audio drops 0 → 10; Intel 528/565 → 553/569 with static audio drops 16 → 0. These are bounded observations, not causal or general throughput improvement.

Intel static measured cold tick 1018.380 → 418.638 ms and 29 → 11 skips; ARM 247.656 → 783.011 ms and 6 → 22 skips. Separate hosted executions and new observer overhead prevent a controlled causal attribution.
No baseline sleep boundary exists. New return lateness observes task resumption against deadline, including executor/host scheduling, not kernel wake/coalescing alone.

Each case has one distinct epoch; canceled returns stay out of successful aggregates. Atomic epoch/reset correctness has separate CPU-only regression evidence. Legacy observer entries may precede rejected production work; loop iteration is not a rendered-frame identity.
Writer-reported audio drops have no retained per-chunk cause/timeline. Healthy video loss, deliberate slow-sink drops, input decoding, warmup and sampled opportunities remain distinct.

Wall minus synchronous caller CPU does not isolate GPU wait; nested spans overlap. Callback peaks contain profiler-only pixel hashing. Endpoint errors are not waveform drift; no resource/hardware/device/network/distribution ceiling is qualified.
